Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 98, verse 1–5:

Tafsir of Surat Lam Yakun (Surah al-Bayyinah)

It is a Madani surah.

The Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad—that is Ibn Salamah—narrated to us, Ali—that is Ibn Zayd—informed us, from Ammar ibn Abi Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Hayyah al-Badri—and he is Malik ibn Amr ibn Thabit al-Ansari—say: When there was revealed, "Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book were not [going to leave]..." to its end, Jibril said: "O Messenger of Allah, indeed your Lord commands you to recite it to Ubayy." So the Prophet ﷺ said to Ubayy: "Indeed Jibril commanded me to recite this surah to you." Ubayy said: "And I was mentioned there, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Yes." He said: So Ubayy wept [[Al-Musnad (3/489).]].

Another narration: And the Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, I heard Qatadah narrating from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Indeed Allah commanded me to recite to you: 'Lam yakun alladhina kafaru'." He said: "And He named me to you?" He said: "Yes." So he wept.

Al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i also narrated it, from the hadith of Shu'bah, with this chain [[Al-Musnad (3/130), Sahih al-Bukhari (4959), Sahih Muslim no. (799), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3792), and Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (11691).]].

Another narration: The Imam Ahmad said: Mu'ammal narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Aslam al-Minqari narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from his father, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Indeed I have been commanded to recite to you the surah such-and-such." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, and I was mentioned there?" He said: "Yes." So I said to him: "O Abu al-Mundhir," and I was delighted by that. He said: "And what would prevent me, when Allah says: 'Say: In the grace of Allah and in His mercy—in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate' [Yunus: 58]." Mu'ammal said: I said to Sufyan: "The recitation in the hadith?" He said: "Yes." He alone transmitted it by this route [[Al-Musnad (5/123).]].

Another route: Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Hajjaj narrated to us, both said: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to me: "Indeed Allah commanded me to recite the Qur'an to you." He said: So he recited: "Lam yakun alladhina kafaru min ahl al-kitab..." He said: In it he recited: "If the son of Adam asked for a valley of wealth, and it were given to him, he would ask for a second; and if he asked for a second and it were given to him, he would ask for a third. And nothing fills the belly of the son of Adam except dust, and Allah accepts the repentance of whoever repents. Indeed that religion with Allah is the hanifiyyah, not polytheistic nor Jewish nor Christian, and whoever does good, it will not be denied him."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Shu'bah, with this chain [[Al-Musnad (5/131) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3793).]], and he said: "Hasan sahih."

Another route: The Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Khulayd al-Halabi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isa al-Tabba' narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Muhammad ibn Mu'adh ibn Ubayy ibn Ka'b narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Abu al-Mundhir, indeed I have been commanded to present the Qur'an to you." He said: "I believe in Allah, I submitted at your hand, and I learned from you." He said: So the Prophet ﷺ repeated the words. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, was I mentioned there?" He said: "Yes, by your name and your lineage in the Highest Assembly." He said: "Then recite, O Messenger of Allah" [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (1/200).]].

This is strange from this route, and what is established is what has preceded. The Prophet ﷺ recited this surah to him only to strengthen him and to increase his faith, for he—as Ahmad and al-Nasa'i narrated, by the route of Anas, from him [[Al-Musnad (5/122) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/54).]]—and Ahmad and Abu Dawud narrated from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Surad, from him [[Al-Musnad (5/124) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1477).]]—and Ahmad narrated from Affan, from Hammad, from Humayd, from Anas, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, from him [[Al-Musnad (5/114).]]—and Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated from the hadith of Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Isa, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from him [[Al-Musnad (5/127), Sahih Muslim no. (820), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1478), and Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/153).]]: he had objected to a man, namely Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, reciting something of the Qur'an contrary to how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had taught him. He raised it to the Prophet ﷺ, who had them both recite, and said to each of them: "You are correct." Ubayy said: "Doubt seized me, even more than in the Jahiliyyah." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ struck him on the chest, and Ubayy said: "I sweated, and it was as if I were looking at Allah in fear." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed him that Jibril had come to him and said: "Indeed Allah commands you to recite to your Ummah the Qur'an in one harf." I said: "I ask Allah for His pardon and forgiveness." He said: "In two harfs." He continued until he said: "Indeed Allah commands you to recite to your Ummah the Qur'an in seven ahruf." As we have already mentioned this hadith with its routes and wordings at the beginning of the tafsir. When this noble surah was revealed, in which is: "A Messenger from Allah, reciting purified scriptures, in which are upright books," the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it to him in a recitation of conveying, establishing and warning, not a recitation of learning and memorising, and Allah knows best.

This is like the case of Umar ibn al-Khattab, when on the day of al-Hudaybiyah he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about those questions, and among what he said was: "Did you not used to tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?" He said: "Yes. Did I inform you that you would come to it this year?" He said: "No." He said: "Then you will come to it and circumambulate it." When they returned from al-Hudaybiyah, and Allah revealed to the Prophet ﷺ the surah "al-Fath," he called Umar ibn al-Khattab and recited it to him, and in it is His saying: "Allah has certainly fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth: you will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in security..." [al-Fath: 27], as has preceded.

Abu Nu'aym al-Hafiz narrated in his book "Asma' al-Sahabah," by the route of Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ja'fari al-Madani: Abdullah ibn Salamah ibn Aslam narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Isma'il ibn Abi Hakim al-Madani, Fudayl narrated to me, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Indeed Allah hears the recitation of 'Lam yakun alladhina kafaru,' and says: 'Rejoice, My servant; by My might, I will surely grant it to you in Paradise until you are pleased.'"

This is a very strange hadith. Al-Hafiz Abu Musa al-Madini and Ibn al-Athir also narrated it, by the route of al-Zuhri, from Isma'il ibn Abi Hakim, from Nazir al-Muzani—or al-Madani—from the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed Allah hears the recitation of 'Lam yakun alladhina kafaru,' and says: 'Rejoice, My servant; by My might, I will never forget you in any state of this world and the Hereafter, and I will surely grant it to you in Paradise until you are pleased.'" [[Usd al-Ghabah by Ibn al-Athir (4/549), and Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned it in al-Isabah (3/528) by the route of Abu Musa, and it is from the route of Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ja'far, from Abdullah ibn Salamah, from al-Zuhri, and he said: "Abdullah ibn Salamah is weak in hadith."]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

* *

As for the People of the Book, they are: the Jews and the Christians. The polytheists are the worshippers of idols and fire, from among the Arabs and the non-Arabs. Mujahid said: "They were not [[munfakkin]]," meaning: "ceasing" until the truth became clear to them. Qatadah said likewise.

"Until there comes to them clear evidence" — that is, this Qur'an. For this reason the Exalted said: "Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to cease until there came to them clear evidence." Then He explained the clear evidence with His saying: "A Messenger from Allah, reciting purified scriptures" — meaning Muhammad ﷺ, and what he recites of the Great Qur'an, which is written in the Highest Assembly, in purified scriptures, like His saying: "In honoured scriptures, exalted and purified, by the hands of scribes, noble and dutiful" [Abasa: 13–16].

* *

And His saying: "in which are upright books" — Ibn Jarir said: That is, in the purified scriptures are books from Allah that are [[qayyimah]]: just and upright, with no error in them, because they are from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Qatadah said: "A Messenger from Allah, reciting purified scriptures" — he mentions the Qur'an in the best of mentions and praises it with the best of praise.

Ibn Zayd said: "in which are upright books" — straight and moderate.

* *

And His saying: "And they were not divided except after the clear evidence came to them" is like His saying: "And do not be like those who divided and differed after the clear proofs had come to them; those will have a great punishment" [Al 'Imran: 105]. By this is meant the People of the Books revealed to the nations before us: after Allah had established proofs and clear evidence against them, they divided and differed concerning what Allah intended from their books, and they differed greatly, as came in the hadith narrated through several routes: "The Jews differed into seventy-one sects, the Christians differed into seventy-two sects, and this Ummah will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one." They said: "Who are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Those who follow what I and my Companions are upon" [[This hadith comes from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, Anas, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Mu'awiyah, Amr ibn Awf al-Muzani, Awf ibn Malik, Abu Umamah, and Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said: "It is a sahih, well-known hadith." See: Takhrij Ahadith al-Kashshaf by al-Zayla'i (1/447–450).]].

* *

And His saying: "And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion, upright" is like His saying: "And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me" [al-Anbiya: 25]. For this reason He said: "hunafa'," that is, turning away from shirk to tawhid. Like His saying: "And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying]: Worship Allah and avoid the taghut" [al-Nahl: 36]. The explanation of "hanif" has already been established in the commentary on surah "al-An'am" [[At the explanation of verse 161.]], sufficiently so that it need not be repeated here.

"And establish prayer" — which is the most noble of the bodily acts of worship — "and give zakah" — which is kindness to the poor and the needy. "And that is the religion of the upright community" — that is, the established, just religion, or: the straight, moderate community.

Many of the imams, such as al-Zuhri and al-Shafi'i, used this noble verse as evidence that actions are part of faith. For this reason He said: "And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion, upright, and to establish prayer and give zakah; and that is the religion of the upright community."

I said: "I ask Allah for His pardon and forgiveness." He said: "In two harfs." He continued until he said: "Indeed Allah commands you to recite to your Ummah the Qur'an in seven ahruf." As we have already mentioned this hadith with its routes and wordings at the beginning of the tafsir. When this noble surah was revealed, in which is: "A Messenger from Allah, reciting purified scriptures, in which are upright books," the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited it to him in a recitation of conveying, establishing and warning, not a recitation of learning and memorising, and Allah knows best.

This is like the case of Umar ibn al-Khattab, when on the day of al-Hudaybiyah he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about those questions, and among what he said was: "Did you not used to tell us that we would come to the House and circumambulate it?" He said: "Yes. Did I inform you that you would come to it this year?" He said: "No." He said: "Then you will come to it and circumambulate it." When they returned from al-Hudaybiyah, and Allah revealed to the Prophet ﷺ the surah "al-Fath," he called Umar ibn al-Khattab and recited it to him, and in it is His saying: "Allah has certainly fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth: you will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if Allah wills, in security..." [al-Fath: 27], as has preceded.

Abu Nu'aym al-Hafiz narrated in his book "Asma' al-Sahabah," by the route of Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ja'fari al-Madani: Abdullah ibn Salamah ibn Aslam narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Isma'il ibn Abi Hakim al-Madani, Fudayl narrated to me, I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Indeed Allah hears the recitation of 'Lam yakun alladhina kafaru,' and says: 'Rejoice, My servant; by My might, I will surely grant it to you in Paradise until you are pleased.'"

This is a very strange hadith. Al-Hafiz Abu Musa al-Madini and Ibn al-Athir also narrated it, by the route of al-Zuhri, from Isma'il ibn Abi Hakim, from Nazir al-Muzani—or al-Madani—from the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed Allah hears the recitation of 'Lam yakun alladhina kafaru,' and says: 'Rejoice, My servant; by My might, I will never forget you in any state of this world and the Hereafter, and I will surely grant it to you in Paradise until you are pleased.'" [[Usd al-Ghabah by Ibn al-Athir (4/549), and Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned it in al-Isabah (3/528) by the route of Abu Musa, and it is from the route of Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Ja'far, from Abdullah ibn Salamah, from al-Zuhri, and he said: "Abdullah ibn Salamah is weak in hadith."]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

* *

As for the People of the Book, they are: the Jews and the Christians. The polytheists are the worshippers of idols and fire, from among the Arabs and the non-Arabs. Mujahid said: "They were not [[munfakkin]]," meaning: "ceasing" until the truth became clear to them. Qatadah said likewise.

"Until there comes to them clear evidence" — that is, this Qur'an. For this reason the Exalted said: "Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not going to cease until there came to them clear evidence." Then He explained the clear evidence with His saying: "A Messenger from Allah, reciting purified scriptures" — meaning Muhammad ﷺ, and what he recites of the Great Qur'an, which is written in the Highest Assembly, in purified scriptures, like His saying: "In honoured scriptures, exalted and purified, by the hands of scribes, noble and dutiful" [Abasa: 13–16].

* *

And His saying: "in which are upright books" — Ibn Jarir said: That is, in the purified scriptures are books from Allah that are [[qayyimah]]: just and upright, with no error in them, because they are from Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Qatadah said: "A Messenger from Allah, reciting purified scriptures" — he mentions the Qur'an in the best of mentions and praises it with the best of praise.

Ibn Zayd said: "in which are upright books" — straight and moderate.

* *

And His saying: "And they were not divided except after the clear evidence came to them" is like His saying: "And do not be like those who divided and differed after the clear proofs had come to them; those will have a great punishment" [Al 'Imran: 105]. By this is meant the People of the Books revealed to the nations before us: after Allah had established proofs and clear evidence against them, they divided and differed concerning what Allah intended from their books, and they differed greatly, as came in the hadith narrated through several routes: "The Jews differed into seventy-one sects, the Christians differed into seventy-two sects, and this Ummah will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one." They said: "Who are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Those who follow what I and my Companions are upon" [[This hadith comes from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, Anas, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Mu'awiyah, Amr ibn Awf al-Muzani, Awf ibn Malik, Abu Umamah, and Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them. Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said: "It is a sahih, well-known hadith." See: Takhrij Ahadith al-Kashshaf by al-Zayla'i (1/447–450).]].

* *

And His saying: "And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion, upright" is like His saying: "And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me" [al-Anbiya: 25]. For this reason He said: "hunafa'," that is, turning away from shirk to tawhid. Like His saying: "And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying]: Worship Allah and avoid the taghut" [al-Nahl: 36]. The explanation of "hanif" has already been established in the commentary on surah "al-An'am" [[At the explanation of verse 161.]], sufficiently so that it need not be repeated here.

"And establish prayer" — which is the most noble of the bodily acts of worship — "and give zakah" — which is kindness to the poor and the needy. "And that is the religion of the upright community" — that is, the established, just religion, or: the straight, moderate community.

Many of the imams, such as al-Zuhri and al-Shafi'i, used this noble verse as evidence that actions are part of faith. For this reason He said: "And they were not commanded except to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion, upright, and to establish prayer and give zakah; and that is the religion of the upright community."

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah, exalted is He, informs about the end of the wicked, from among the disbelievers of the People of the Book and the polytheists who opposed the revealed Books of Allah and the sent Prophets of Allah: that on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿they will abide forever in the Fire of Hell﴾, meaning they will remain there, not being moved from it nor departing from it. ﴿Those are the worst of creation﴾, meaning the worst of the creatures whom Allah brought into being and created.

Then Allah informs about the state of the righteous, those who believed in their hearts and did righteous deeds with their bodies, that they are ﴿the best of creation﴾.

Abu Hurayrah and a group of scholars used this verse as evidence for the superiority of believing humans (al-bariyyah) over the angels, based on His saying: ﴿Those are the best of creation﴾.

Then He said: ﴿Their reward with their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence (Jannat 'Adn), beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever﴾, meaning, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿forever﴾, meaning without cutting off, without ending, and without exhaustion.

﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him.﴾ The station of His being pleased with them is higher than what they have been given of lasting bliss. ﴿And they are pleased with Him﴾ for what He has granted them of abundant grace.

* *

His saying: ﴿That is for whoever fears his Lord﴾, meaning this reward is attained by whoever fears Allah and is conscious of Him with the consciousness due to Him, and worships Him as though he sees Him, knowing that if he does not see Him, He indeed sees him.

Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn 'Isa narrated to us, Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Abu Wahb, the freedman of Abu Hurayrah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not inform you of the best of creation?" They said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "A man who holds the bridle of his horse in the way of Allah; whenever there is an alarm, he mounts it. Shall I not inform you of the best of creation?" They said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "A man in a flock of his sheep, who establishes the prayer and gives the zakat. Shall I not inform you of the worst of creation?" They said: Yes. He said: "The one who is asked by Allah's name, yet gives nothing when asked by it."

[Musnad (2/396); al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id (5/279): "Abu Ma'shar (Najih) is weak, and Abu Ma'shar (as it stands there; the correct reading is Abu Wahb), the freedman of Abu Hurayrah, I do not know him."]

End of the tafsir of Surah "Lam Yakun".
